variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system is an application pipeline that finds external evidence for a question, places selected evidence in a language model's context, and asks the model to answer from that evidence.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Separate the knowledge loop from the answer loop”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Ingest sources
pairs.detail: Discover authorized documents, parse structure, normalize text, and attach source, revision, owner, access, and freshness metadata.
pairs.explanation: Discover authorized documents, parse structure, normalize text, and attach source, revision, owner, access, and freshness metadata.

pairs.label: Publish an index
pairs.detail: Chunk content, compute versioned representations, write searchable records, verify counts, then atomically publish one snapshot.
pairs.explanation: Chunk content, compute versioned representations, write searchable records, verify counts, then atomically publish one snapshot.

pairs.label: Retrieve candidates
pairs.detail: Authorize the request before search, encode or rewrite the query, and collect lexical, dense, or structured candidates.
pairs.explanation: Authorize the request before search, encode or rewrite the query, and collect lexical, dense, or structured candidates.

pairs.label: Rerank evidence
pairs.detail: Deduplicate, apply metadata and safety filters, and spend a bounded second-stage budget on the strongest candidates.
pairs.explanation: Deduplicate, apply metadata and safety filters, and spend a bounded second-stage budget on the strongest candidates.

pairs.label: Assemble and answer
pairs.detail: Fit source-labeled evidence into the prompt budget and require supported claims, claim-linked citations, and abstention.
pairs.explanation: Fit source-labeled evidence into the prompt budget and require supported claims, claim-linked citations, and abstention.

pairs.label: Verify and contain
pairs.detail: Check policy, support, freshness, citations, latency, and cost before serving; otherwise abstain, degrade, or route to review.
pairs.explanation: Check policy, support, freshness, citations, latency, and cost before serving; otherwise abstain, degrade, or route to review.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. RAG matters when an application needs private, domain-specific, or changing knowledge.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Ingest sources: Discover authorized documents, parse structure, normalize text, and attach source, revision, owner, access, and freshness metadata. Rerank evidence: Deduplicate, apply metadata and safety filters, and spend a bounded second-stage budget on the strongest candidates. Assemble and answer: Fit source-labeled evidence into the prompt budget and require supported claims, claim-linked citations, and abstention. Verify and contain: Check policy, support, freshness, citations, latency, and cost before serving; otherwise abstain, degrade, or route to review.

variants.title: Make the decision
variants.context: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system is an application pipeline that finds external evidence for a question, places selected evidence in a language model's context, and asks the model to answer from that evidence.
variants.prompt: What is the core production invariant of a RAG answer?
options: Every factual claim can be traced to authorized, versioned evidence or the system abstains
The generator always receives the maximum context window
Dense retrieval always returns more documents than sparse retrieval
The model answers from parametric memory whenever retrieval is slow
variants.explanation: RAG is trustworthy only when evidence identity, authorization, freshness, and claim support survive through the answer. Missing support should trigger containment, not invention.

variants.prompt: Why can hybrid retrieval outperform dense-only retrieval for a product-support corpus?
options: Lexical search preserves exact codes while dense search captures paraphrased meaning
Hybrid retrieval removes the need for authorization filters
It guarantees every retrieved chunk is factually correct
It makes reranking and evaluation unnecessary

variants.prompt: Why should freshness and deletion tests be release gates rather than dashboard-only metrics?

Keep the old document vectors but use the new query encoder

variants.prompt: A retrieved web page says to ignore system instructions and disclose secrets. How should the RAG pipeline treat it?
options: As untrusted data that is screened, isolated, and quarantined when suspicious
As a higher-priority instruction because retrieval selected it
As safe if its similarity score is above the threshold
As safe when it has a citation URL
variants.explanation: Retrieval relevance is not authority. Indirect prompt injection can arrive through indexed content, so suspicious evidence must not control application instructions or tools.
